part.name: Corded cylindrical appliance housing with support yoke
part.description: Multi-solid assembly consisting of a large rounded rectangular/cylindrical enclosure, end and rear panels, an external U-shaped support yoke, internal cylindrical drum and liner components, a central handle and spindle, two lower terminal blocks, and an attached power cord with two-pin plug. STEP report contains 20 solids and 414 faces; major-face matches are based on surface type, size, position, and bounding-box correlation with the rendered views.
part.symmetry_note: The principal enclosure, yoke, internal drum, spindle, and lower terminal blocks are approximately bilaterally symmetric about the longitudinal center plane. The power cord and plug break this symmetry, and several rear-panel details are slightly asymmetric.

Section.name: Main enclosure and end-panel system
Section.function intent: Enclose and protect the working components, provide the dominant appliance form, locate end panels, and provide lateral interfaces for the external support yoke.
Section.physical behavior: The broad shell carries distributed handling and support loads as membrane and bending stress. Rounded longitudinal shoulders reduce edge stress and improve stiffness. End plates close the enclosure and brace the shell against racking, while the lateral apertures react pivot or clamping loads from the yoke.
Section.geometry: A long rounded rectangular shell with a broad curved lower surface, planar side bands, large flat end closures, radiused upper shoulders, and supplementary thin end/fascia plates. Several stepped panel layers occur near the rear/top end.
Section.location: Dominant central body extending along the long axis of the part.

Section.name: Perforated rear insert and internal grille
Section.function intent: Provide a ventilated or guarded rear interface while retaining components and distributing local panel loads around numerous openings.
Section.physical behavior: The thin profiled plate behaves primarily in membrane and local bending. Repeated ribs between slots stiffen the panel, while the curved perimeter transfers load into the surrounding enclosure. Multiple openings permit airflow or clearance while preventing direct access to internal parts.
Section.geometry: Two closely related thin profiled solids occupying the same rear region, each with many rectangular cutouts or ribs, planar front and rear faces, a broad curved lower edge, and short perimeter facets.
Section.location: At the rear/top end of the enclosure, immediately inside or behind the outer fascia.

Section.name: Internal cylindrical drum and annular liner
Section.function intent: Provide the principal internal cylindrical cavity or working chamber and locate the axial spindle and associated internal component.
Section.physical behavior: The concentric cylindrical walls resist radial pressure, contact, or component loads through hoop stiffness. Annular end faces maintain circularity and transmit axial loads into the enclosure. Stepped diameters provide assembly location and running clearance.
Section.geometry: A nested set of coaxial cylindrical and annular solids with several radii, planar annular ends, stepped shoulders, and two local rectangular pad features.
Section.location: Inside the main enclosure, centered on the internal transverse axis visible through the top opening.

Section.name: Internal cylindrical cartridge and top handle
Section.function intent: Provide a removable or serviceable cylindrical internal element and a grip for lifting, positioning, or extracting it from the enclosure.
Section.physical behavior: The cylindrical cartridge maintains shape through hoop stiffness and bears against surrounding annular supports. The rectangular handle carries hand-applied force in bending and transfers it through two end supports into the cartridge wall.
Section.geometry: A central hollow cylinder with stepped annular end geometry and a narrow rectangular U-like handle spanning above its upper surface.
Section.location: Centered within the top access opening and inside the larger drum.

Section.name: Central spindle and stepped shaft
Section.function intent: Locate the internal cylindrical components on a common axis, constrain radial motion, and transmit limited axial or rotational loads.
Section.physical behavior: The shaft carries shear, bending, and possible torsional loads. Diameter steps and annular shoulders react axial displacement, while toroidal blends reduce stress concentration between adjacent diameters.
Section.geometry: A long stepped cylindrical spindle with several concentric diameter changes, annular planar ends, and toroidal transition radii.
Section.location: On the center axis of the internal drum and cartridge.

Section.name: Internal curved handle or retaining plate
Section.function intent: Provide a secondary grip, retainer, or structural bridge over an internal circular component.
Section.physical behavior: The plate behaves as a curved beam. Its broad faces carry bending stress, while the side legs transfer load to adjacent supports. The cylindrical crown distributes contact and reduces sharp stress transitions.
Section.geometry: A thick, flat-sided curved plate with a semicircular crown and two descending side regions.
Section.location: Inside the upper access region, spanning above the internal cylindrical assembly.

Section.physical behavior: The block transfers finger or contact force through short planar walls into the supporting panel. Its compact section gives high local stiffness but concentrates load at the attachment face.

Section.name: Twin lower terminal blocks
Section.function intent: Provide two discrete lower connection or mounting interfaces, likely for electrical terminals, feet, or attachment posts.
Section.physical behavior: Each block transfers concentrated contact or connector loads into the enclosure. Rounded corner cylinders reduce snagging and local edge stress, while broad end faces provide seating and contact area.
Section.geometry: A mirrored pair of small rectangular prismatic blocks with rounded corners and stepped upper portions.
Section.location: On the lower front edge of the enclosure, visible as two small symmetric projections.

Section.name: External U-shaped support yoke
Section.function intent: Support or suspend the main enclosure, permit limited pivoting about two lateral mounting points, and distribute the enclosure weight through a wide curved cradle.
Section.physical behavior: The yoke behaves as a curved beam under bending. Loads enter through the two pivot bores, travel down the upright arms, and are distributed around the lower curved span. The wide rectangular section resists lateral twist and bending.
Section.geometry: A thick U-shaped plate with parallel planar faces, straight upper arms, a broad curved lower bridge, and coaxial circular bores through the arm ends.
Section.location: Outside the enclosure, wrapping around its lower front/back profile with one arm on each side.

Section.name: Flexible power cord and strain-relief region
Section.function intent: Transmit electrical power between the external plug and internal appliance terminals while allowing flexible routing and movement.
Section.physical behavior: The cable bends along a smooth spatial curve and carries axial tension with low bending stiffness. The enlarged or constrained exit region limits sharp curvature and transfers pull loads into the enclosure rather than directly into conductors.
Section.geometry: A long narrow swept body with a complex BSpline route, approximately constant thickness, locally flattened side faces, and a short straight attachment segment at the enclosure.
Section.location: Exits the lower enclosure and hangs externally in an S-shaped curve toward the plug.

Section.name: Two-pin mains plug
Section.function intent: Provide the detachable electrical interface to an external mains receptacle and protect the conductor terminations.
Section.physical behavior: The molded body supports insertion and extraction loads and electrically isolates the conductors. The two pins carry contact force and current, while the cable-entry region transfers tensile and bending loads into the plug body.
Section.geometry: A small faceted molded body at the cable end with an angled profile and two narrow projecting prismatic pins.
Section.location: At the free end of the external power cord.
